title: Bar chart does not display for one column data if there is a '.' in the column name
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Bar chart does not display for one column data if there is a '.' in the column name.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7714)

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np

st.title("This works")
chart_data = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(20, 3), columns=["a", "b", "c"])
st.bar_chart(chart_data)

st.title("This works")
chart_data = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(20, 3), columns=["a.b", "b.c", "c.d"])
st.bar_chart(chart_data)

st.title("This works")
chart_data = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(20, 1), columns=["a"])
st.bar_chart(chart_data)

st.title("This doesn't work")
chart_data = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(20, 1), columns=["a.b"])
st.bar_chart(chart_data)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run this
2. Note the cases which do and do not display a graph

### Expected Behavior

There should be four graphs.

### Current Behavior

There are only three being displayed properly.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.28.1
- Python version: 3.10.12
- Operating System: 5.15.0-88-generic #98-Ubuntu
- Browser: Chrome Version 119.0.6045.123 (Official Build) (arm64)


### Additional Information

I suspect that there is somewhere in the code confusing the '.' in the column name for the dot operator. I expect that '.'s need to be escaped. Not sure why this only happens with one column and not with multiple columns.

Hey [USER]!

Thank you for reporting this issue, I was able to reproduce it and can confirm that this is a bug. 

Issue demo link: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-7714
I can add to this that it also does not work for labels that contain square brackets, i.e. `"CO₂ Storage [t]"`

This repros for all Altair-backed charts (bar, line, scatter, area), not just bar charts. This is because [the field parameter we pass in](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/38251aad1c2615ee8c100144f2e04eb9f26f1fd3/lib/streamlit/elements/arrow_altair.py#L1303) is sourced directly from the column name, [but _only_ for the non-"melted" case](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/38251aad1c2615ee8c100144f2e04eb9f26f1fd3/lib/streamlit/elements/arrow_altair.py#L1291-L1300), and we only "melt" [in the multi-column case](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/38251aad1c2615ee8c100144f2e04eb9f26f1fd3/lib/streamlit/elements/arrow_altair.py#L1208-L1227). The reason this breaks things is Altair treats string fields with dots as nested field access; see [these encoding docs](https://altair-viz.github.io/altair-viz-v4/user_guide/encoding.html): Note that the solution is a simple escape.
Unsurprisingly this also breaks with brackets (e.g. `columns=["a[b]"]` in the example code).

After playing around with this for a bit, escaping does _not_ seem to fix the underlying issue - at least for columns with dots in the name. There are also open bugs like [this one](https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/issues/7066) in vega-lite, which makes me think escaping simply isn't implemented correctly.

I think the right solution here is to use a uniqueified column name in all cases, not just the melted case. I'm going to unassign this until I have time to investigate that solution.
